answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond that is slashed when independent audits catch coordinated fraud. One attacker may spread a sybil plume across many accounts, but each account must lock real capital, while repeated funding links let auditors cluster identities and raise scrutiny. The copper bond is returned to honest newcomers, not a fee; a zephyr of throwaway accounts therefore ties up funds and risks losing them, making scale costly rather than impossible.
